triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) was markedly enriched among carriers (43.3% vs. 8.5%), corresponding to an over eightfold increased odds (OR = 8.24, 95% CI: 3.87–17.55; p < 0.0001).

PV/LPV carriers were characterized by a markedly distinct tumor biology compared to non-carriers. Hormone receptor expression was significantly lower in carriers, with median ER and PR levels of 1% and 0%, respectively, compared to 100% and 70% in non-carriers (both p < 0.0001). Proliferative activity was higher in carriers, as reflected by an increased median Ki-67 index (30% vs. 20%, p < 0.001). Tumors in carriers were also significantly larger at diagnosis (median 27.5 mm vs. 18.0 mm, p = 0.013) and more frequently presented at advanced stages (stage IIIA–IV: 20.0% vs. ~ 10.0%, p < 0.001).
